method: Reuse each revision trial's private target, add one non-inlined native function, then change its numeric return value twice. Sequential incremental then artifact-only arms, separate Kache runtime/configuration, shared object store, and the same embedding probe. Source revision metadata is deliberately held constant while real Rust source commits change.
interpretation: Retained incremental state also reduces native compiler work after the measured function-body edits. Positive and negative probes reach the compiled native function, so revision-only metadata reuse cannot explain the result. The retained incremental target consumes about 8.8 GiB versus 3.8 GiB for the artifact target.
limitations: Two tiny function-body edits per arm, not a representative distribution of large source changes. The arms are not interleaved and other leased work can run on the shared host.
The first function-addition command includes capacity lease wait; its 96.60-second native compiler unit must not be confused with its 155.82-second command wall time.
This probe uses the native default feature set. The canonical CLI also enables otel and links the CLI and host libraries, which remain unmeasured here.
The targets already contain incremental/artifact state from the revision trial. This is not a cold-bootstrap or cross-target restore result.

Kache reports are cumulative checkout sessions. Incremental native compiles are passthroughs whose compiler time is absent from cache timing totals; Cargo unit sections and command wall times provide the timing evidence.
No CI behavior is changed by this record. The ten-minute merge-group goal remains unproven.
